name: Azerbaijan

findings.summary: Deputy digital minister said AzInTelecom deployed AI infrastructure built on 32 Nvidia H200 GPUs; reporting says procurement of further GPUs to expand the centre is under way. No value disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole us: Nvidia supplies the accelerators. JAMnews says Lenovo supplied the underlying server infrastructure; Lenovo's controller pole (Hong Kong/Beijing HQ) is ambiguous and not coded separately. All three opened sources are S3 (Report.az and Trend are Azerbaijani outlets generally seen as government-friendly), so no S1/S2 and not corroborated. Small (32-GPU) deployment, but it is the national AI compute facility.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Digital Development and Transport
findings.summary: AzInTelecom set up Azerbaijan's first supercomputer centre for AI work by innovators, businesses and government projects, framed as letting state data be processed domestically under the 2025-2028 AI strategy.
findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator is state-linked AzInTelecom, so domestic. Building size, power and builder not reported. Pairs with AZE-001 (same site, silicon layer).

findings.summary: The 2026-2028 digital development action plan provides for a National Supercomputing Centre led by AzInTelecom; foreign partners, capacity, data handling and export-control questions remain open.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1: a government plan item, no contract or construction reported. Date is the action-plan period start; JAMnews article dated 2026-06-24. Whether it supersedes or expands the Dec 2025 centre is unclear.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Digital Development and Transport
findings.summary: The digital ministry signed a memorandum with SpaceXAI to explore Grok-based AI for public services across government institutions, including mygov, with a roadmap of pilots; specific projects need separate agreements.
findings.analyst_inference: Grok would be used via the provider's service, so us pole. Tier 1 MoU, no value. Only one opened source. Reviewer may wish to confirm the counterparty name and corporate status of 'SpaceXAI' from a primary source.

findings.summary: After a Baku 5G pilot zone, Azercell and Ericsson signed a three-year 5G MoU for 2020-22 covering further pilots, use cases and IoT; Azercell was still preparing its 5G licence application in October 2022.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson is Swedish, so third pole. Tier 1 non-binding MoU; MoU term has lapsed and no commercial 5G vendor award for Azercell was found. Azercell's 4G RAN and core vendor not established. Pre-2020.

findings.summary: Bakcell completed a core-network unification project with Huawei, moving all voice traffic onto new redundant LTE-ready switching, after modernising its transmission network with Huawei OSN equipment earlier in 2013.
findings.analyst_inference: Operator's own release, coded S1. Huawei as equipment vendor, so prc. Pre-2020 and still_current unknown: no evidence found on Bakcell's current core or RAN vendor or 5G supplier.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Digital Development and Transport; ADA University
findings.summary: The digital ministry, ADA University and Huawei signed an MoU for a joint R&D centre for ICT products and Huawei-certified training of local specialists in 5G, GPON and IP technologies.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Digital Development and Transport

findings.analyst_inference: Signing date not stated on the page (date null). Mainly skills and R&D, not deployment; coded networks as the named technologies are network ones.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Digital Development and Transport
findings.summary: The digital minister and a Huawei senior vice-president discussed raising cooperation to a strategic partnership, with possible joint AI, data-centre, 5G and cloud projects and a possible Huawei regional operations centre; no agreement reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Discussion only, below even an MoU; tier 1 is the floor. Layer networks chosen because 5G/cloud dominate; it spans facilities and cloud. Notable alongside AZE-004 as a near-simultaneous approach from both poles.

findings.summary: Laying began on the 380 km, 400 Tbps Trans-Caspian subsea cable from Sumgait to Aktau, built by Azertelecom and Kazakhtelecom's CaspiLink JV under US-based Pioneer Consulting's supervision; commissioning targeted end-2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: under the v0.2 rule a cable's controller is its equipment vendor, and no source names the cable supplier or installer (no HMN Tech mention). Value and financier undisclosed. Part of the Digital Silk Way corridor; Developing Telecoms also links it to China's Digital Silk Road, which is a framing, not evidence of PRC control.

applications.null_reason: one dedicated search found no Azerbaijan-specific safe-city or surveillance vendor reporting; results concerned other countries

power.null_reason: no AI- or data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced in other searches

research_gaps: Who supplied Azercell's and Bakcell's commercial 5G RAN and core (Ericsson, Nokia, Huawei, ZTE), and what does Nar (Azerfon) use?
Vendor of Baku's public CCTV / 'safe city' system (Ministry of Internal Affairs) and whether it has facial recognition.
Cable supplier and marine installer for the Trans-Caspian cable (CaspiLink), and its financing.
Lenovo's role at the AzInTelecom supercomputer centre and size of the follow-on GPU procurement; any BIS licence for H200s.
Primary-source confirmation of the SpaceXAI MoU, and any Microsoft, OpenAI or other model-provider agreements with the government.
